# Plugin transport (engine <-> plugin): current flow digest

<!-- LIVING digest: the current shape of this subsystem. Update it when you change the subsystem. -->
<!-- Generated by tracing the code; verify file:line before relying on a detail. -->
<!-- digest-base: internal/component/plugin pkg/plugin internal/core/events pkg/ze -->

## What it is
The bidirectional message layer between the ze engine and its plugins. Every plugin runs the SDK (`pkg/plugin/sdk`) over a single bidirectional connection and, after a 5-stage RPC startup, uses one of two transports: JSON-RPC over a socket (external plugins) or an in-process `DirectBridge` of typed Go function calls with no JSON/socket (internal plugins). Sitting on top is the typed pub/sub `EventBus` (`pkg/ze.EventBus`), where the engine emits events down and plugins send commands/RPCs up.

## Flow

**(1) Engine event → plugin (down).** A publisher calls a typed handle `Event[T].Emit(bus, payload)` (`internal/core/events/typed.go:100`) → `bus.Emit` → `Server.Emit` (`server/engine_event.go:157`) → `EmitEngineEvent` (`engine_event.go:150`) → `Server.deliverEvent(nil, ns, et, …)` (`server/dispatch.go:199`). deliverEvent validates `(ns,et)` via `events.IsValidEvent`, matches plugin-process subscribers with `s.subscriptions.GetMatching` (`server/dispatch.go:249`), marshals the payload to JSON once and lazily via `payloadToJSON` (`server/dispatch.go:286`, only when an external subscriber exists), and enqueues `p.Deliver(EventDelivery{Output: eventJSON})` (`server/dispatch.go:269`). It also `defer`s `dispatchEngineEvent` (`server/dispatch.go:243`) to fire in-process engine handlers after plugin delivery. `Process.Deliver` (`process/delivery.go:66`) queues onto `eventChan`; `deliveryLoop` (`delivery.go:108`) batches and calls `sendBatch` (`delivery.go:248`), which picks bridge-structured (`deliverMixedBatch`→`bridge.DeliverStructured`), bridge-text (`bridge.DeliverEvents`, `rpc/bridge.go:225`), or socket (`deliverViaConn`→`conn.SendDeliverBatch`). Plugin side: the bridge invokes the SDK `onEvent(string)` handler wired at `sdk/sdk.go:388`; external plugins receive the `ze-plugin-callback:deliver-batch` callback in `eventLoop` (`sdk/sdk_dispatch.go:215`).

**(2) Plugin command/RPC → engine (up).** The SDK calls e.g. `Plugin.DispatchCommand` (`sdk/sdk_engine.go:170`) or `EmitEvent`/`UpdateRoute`/`ForwardCached`. Each first tries a typed bridge fast path (`bridge.HasDispatchCommand()` → `bridge.DispatchCommand`); otherwise `callEngineRaw` (`sdk/sdk.go:448`) routes to `bridge.DispatchRPC(method, params)` (in-process) or `engineMux.CallRPC` (socket). The method string is an `rpc.Method*` constant (`pkg/plugin/rpc/types.go`) shared with the engine registry. Engine socket side: `handleSingleProcessCommandsRPC` read loop (`server/dispatch.go:57`) → `dispatchPluginRPC` (`server/dispatch.go:79`) resolves `req.Method` through the unified engine-op registry (`lookupEngineOp`, `dispatch_registry.go`) → `serveEngineOpJSON` → the op's shared `handle` → `s.dispatcher.Dispatch(cmdCtx, cmd)`; unknown methods fall through to the codec registry then a fail-closed error. Engine bridge side: `dispatchPluginRPCDirect` (`server/dispatch.go:366`) runs the same registry lookup via `serveEngineOpDirect` and returns `json.RawMessage` directly with no socket I/O.

**(3) In-process DirectBridge typed call.** After Stage 5, `wireBridgeDispatch` (`server/dispatch.go:522`) registers the engine handlers on the bridge: generic `SetDispatchRPC`, plus the typed fast paths installed by iterating `engineOps` and calling each entry's `typedWire` descriptor (not a hand-written list) -- `SetEmitEvent`, `SetDispatchCommand`, `SetDispatchCommandArgs`, `SetUpdateRouteSel`, `SetForwardCached`, `SetReleaseCached`, `SetInjectWireRoute`, `SetBatchValidate`. The SDK registers its side (`SetDeliverEvents`/`SetDeliverStructured`/`SetExecuteCommand`) and calls `SetReady` (`sdk/sdk.go:407`). Engine→plugin callbacks (execute-command, config, bye) flow through `callbackCh`/`executeCommandCh` (`rpc/bridge.go`), drained serially by `bridgeEventLoop` (`sdk/sdk_dispatch.go:184`). Every typed handler is guarded by `HasX() == ready.Load() && hasX.Load()`.

## Invariants & gotchas
- **Registration is `init()`-time.** Each internal plugin's `register.go` `init()` calls `registry.Register`; `all/all.go` blank-imports it. Command/family/capability conflicts are detected at registration (`registration.go:177`) and abort startup.
- **Two transports, one dispatch switch.** External = JSON-RPC over socket (`engineMux`/`PluginConn`); internal = `DirectBridge`. The plugin requests `Transport="bridge"` in the Stage-5 ready RPC (`sdk/sdk.go:363`) and the engine switches `PluginConn` to it (`startup.go:783`). Nil bridge ⇒ socket fallback everywhere.
- **Startup always runs on sockets.** Only the runtime hot path uses the bridge; the 5-stage handshake stays on the pipe (cold path, per retired summary 294; see `plan/learned/DESIGN-HISTORY.md`, "Plugin system: architecture").
- **Wire-before-ready race fix.** `wireBridgeDispatch` MUST run before the engine sends the Stage-5 ready OK, because the SDK calls `SetReady()` immediately after (`startup.go:726` comment; else the SDK takes the bridge path before the engine handler exists).
- **Bridge readiness is atomic.** Every typed setter stores a `hasX atomic.Bool` to publish a happens-before edge; `DispatchRPC`/`DeliverEvents` error out when not ready.
- **Bridge-mode plugins skip the mux read loop.** `handleSingleProcessCommandsRPC` checks `conn.HasBridge()` and blocks on `ctx.Done()` (`server/dispatch.go:47`); reading the mux would return `ErrMuxConnClosed` and wrongly trigger `cleanupProcess`/daemon shutdown during startup.
- **EventBus type registration is the single source of truth.** `events.Register[T](ns, et)` records the `reflect.Type`; empty/interface/duplicate-with-different-type payloads panic at `init` (`typed.go:173`). Consumers never type-assert, the `Event[T].Subscribe` wrapper does, logging a warn on mismatch.
- **`(ns,et)` must be registered.** `deliverEvent` rejects unknown pairs (`events.IsValidEvent`, `server/dispatch.go:205`) and delivers to nobody. Engine *subscriptions* are NOT validated (dead until a matching emit) so dynamically-registered per-plugin event types work.
- **In-process vs external payload.** In-process subscribers get the publisher's Go value directly (zero serialization); external processes get JSON marshaled at most once per Emit. A string emitted via RPC is lazily decoded to the typed value for engine subscribers via `tryDecodeTypedPayload` (`server/dispatch.go:316`).
- **Self-delivery is excluded**, the emitting process is skipped in plugin fan-out (`server/dispatch.go:266`).
- **`StructuredEvent` is pooled and async-unsafe.** It carries zero-copy wire buffers; plugins MUST copy anything they retain past the handler. The delivery loop returns SEs via `PutStructuredEvent` (`delivery.go:200`); a retained reference races with reuse.
- **Two subscriber registries, one `deliverEvent`.** `SubscriptionManager` (plugin processes, direction+peer filtering) and `engineEventSubscribers` (in-process Go, no filtering). Engine handlers run in a `defer` after plugin delivery and survive plugin panics.
- **`subscribe-events` RPC carries no namespace.** It defaults to `plugin.DefaultEventNamespace()` ("bgp"); if unset the namespace is Unknown and subscriptions silently never match (warn logged, `server/dispatch.go:150`).
